notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — Thank You
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/6353d5c572cc7b0857681b86f0e31173adeda862.jpg[/img]

It’s been a week since HOMESICKNESS launched, and the reception has genuinely exceeded my expectations. Throughout the past year of constant, consistent, and continuous development on this project, a lot of doubts came to mind. Doubts about how effective it would be, how many people would resonate with its themes and story, and a variety of other things.

I’m genuinely beyond grateful for all the support and reception. Though this game is still relatively niche, I truly appreciate it. Seeing and reading through reviews, comments, and messages from people who resonated with the game and enjoyed something I spent the past year solely developing has been heartwarming and has meant a lot to me.

I'm still working hard and continuously on this project. I’m focused on helping it reach other spaces, and I have a couple of extra updates planned down the line though nothing huge. One of which being the soundtrack release (Should come out sometime soon, though bare with me). I just wanted to make a brief post to thank everyone for the support and attention I’ve received. One of my core intentions beyond sales was to make a game that could resonate and bring joy, and it appears I’ve succeeded.

Of course, it isn’t over just yet. I’ve got future plans for future projects and a couple of other ideas that are, as of right now, being conceptualized in my mind. I just wanted to thank everyone and let you guys know work isn’t over just yet. I’m keeping an eye out for future reviews, and I look forward to being able to make more stuff in the future.

Do be sure to spread the word around, and I’ll be on the lookout! More updates later down the line—likely adding in a couple of new achievements through Steam, and future patches if anything does happen to come up. Thank you for everything, here's to hoping this game can reach more people along the way. :)

As a way to close off this post, I’d like to thank my friends, family, and the content creators who’ve been looking out for my project. And thank you to everyone for purchasing, sending kind messages, and sharing your thoughts and criticism. It genuinely means a lot.

It isn't over just yet.

notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — Patchnotes (5/26 - 6/1)
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/0abb5a92b00ff09bd846dfd6d9638e8f13d006c8.png[/img]

Hello everyone!

I wanted to go over some of the recent patches I have been actively working on; for those unaware. There is a lot to go over, and there are specifics I could have forgotten, But this is it so far;

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/b860a138decf00de92c9247dbf8b1eedf9a973dc.png[/img]

[b]1.0.1 - 1.0.8[/b]

- Improved lockpad. Now upon discovering a spot locked up with a lockpad, a small lockpad icon will show up exactly where the door is located.

- Fixed an issue where the Telechord would break upon having the UI setting off.

- Performance improvements to Discord Rich Presence and Steamworks API.

- Major fixes to the four pages side mission; reported to me through the Community Hub (Discussions).

- Other minor fixes and polish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/f83925e5f0591f8a19acbd589b0c61976b093398.png[/img]

I wanted to briefly thank everyone for the support and love given to this project. It has meant lots to me, and has served as a significant motivation boost for up and coming plans I'd like to invest into.

It honestly means the world. Hearing people resonate with the game, dropping genuine heartfelt reviews and such, and receiving love from across different spaces online has been great to see.

Thank you for your love for this project, and do be sure to share the word around! Reviews are open for anyone to share their thoughts. I'll be keeping an eye out, and be sure to keep an eye out too for a later post going over a couple of other things! :)

notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — Game is now out!
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=K3LozeP8rpw;full][/previewyoutube]
Hello everyone! I wanted to leave a couple of additional thoughts here regarding this game, now that it is live for everyone to play.

Post-launch, I have a couple of potential update ideas for later down the line, alongside the itch.io page getting a significant update and the game receiving a proper launch in there too, but that, updates alike, will be later down the line. Likely a couple of days, or a few weeks after release. 

These potential update ideas are more-so for added content and for fun, rather than heavily required updates. Though, I'll be keeping an eye out for potential patches if any are to be required.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/b860a138decf00de92c9247dbf8b1eedf9a973dc.png[/img]

A huge chunk of my overall final thoughts can be found in the game itself upon completion, as I’ve decided to write down a couple of developer entries sharing some of my thoughts on this project. But as a final note, at least for now after release, I’d simply like to say thank you to everyone.

I couldn’t have pulled this off without the help and support of a considerable portion of my friends, family, and the people looking out for my project. 

Though I don’t view it as perfect, and there were a lot of sacrifices that had to be made, I ultimately hope this is a game that everyone will be able to connect with and deeply resonate with to some extent after the finish mark.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/f83925e5f0591f8a19acbd589b0c61976b093398.png[/img]

I’ve put a lot of thought into it as the sole developer. I’ve poured tons of time, patience, conflict, struggle, and personal experiences into every inch of this project, and I hope everyone enjoys it!

There’s a lot more I have planned for myself as a developer, and future plans I’d like to see come to fruition. But we’ll see about that in the future.

As of right now, I am happy with the state of this project, and simply know I’ve tried my absolute best all the way through. This has been a crazy journey—two very long years of constant, active development. But it has all paid off, and I couldn’t be happier about it. 

Here’s to hoping this game lives up to expectations. Thank you for everything, and have fun playing! I'll be keeping an eye out. :)

notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — May: Gone Gold
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/dfc1484814d6914958b9ebc1abd3ac492127c2c6.png[/img]

Hello everyone! Jane (celesware) writing this time for a change, as jnity is very hard at work to bring you the game this month! That's right, HOMESICKNESS is scheduled to release this May. Not giving out specifics yet, as it's a little too soon for that, but keep an eye out for that later this month.

So, with that being said, it'll probably be of no surprise to any of you to hear that the game has officially gone gold! Technically, the game can be played from start to finish and all the content that's supposed to be there can be accessed with no issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/012e078b55de1158df4d00f54764c22f1774c6dd.png[/img]

All that's left now is extra polish and balancing, as the final areas are undergoing playtesting and feedback is being gathered. Once that's done, final playtesting and QA checks will be done to ensure the game is ready for shipping. The finish line is closer than ever now.

So, as we are nearing release, I would like to leave some closing thoughts on my behalf as well. HOMESICKNESS, as you all may know, is a solo developed game by jnity, and while my contributions have been largely to varying degrees, this game still means a lot to me, and it feels so incredibly weird yet gratifying to see the finish line approaching now after about a year of seeing the game progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/7f541d538270ecffd6b692f69cd5cae1370db8c5.png[/img]

I would like to thank each and every one of you for not only wishlisting, but also showing interest and supporting the game, it seriously means a lot, not just to me. And to all of you playing the game once it's out, I hope you guys enjoy the game as much just as I loved watching its growth :)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/b860a138decf00de92c9247dbf8b1eedf9a973dc.png[/img]

TLDR: Game's gone gold, final phases of development have begun, game is scheduled to release this May.

notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — April: Nearing Release
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/5558c05939256db2116345d4e8e8b2999d16ac32.png[/img]

Hello everyone! I want to keep up the consistency with monthly updates, and there’s a lot to go over this time.

First, I just want to thank everyone for wishlisting (224+). I know I’ve said this before, but it really does mean a lot to me. After working on this game almost daily for about a year and a half, doubts naturally creep in about how it will be received once it's out.

So seeing people genuinely excited, invested in this project, and appreciating what I’ve been creating means more than you can imagine, even if it turns out to be a small group. Regardless, thank you so much!

On bigger news, specifically regarding the game's overall development and recent progress, I’ve got some updates!

[previewyoutube=i8DvCvPQoI4;full][/previewyoutube]

Since the last Opener post, I can now safely say that the game’s content and mechanics are fully complete! Playtesting over the past month has gone well, and I’ve been focused on polishing every detail to the best of my ability. 

There’s still some work left, with one of the most notable tasks being room modeling, which will begin soon. That’s the final major step before I can officially say HOMESICKNESS has gone gold!

As I mentioned in the Opener post, my rough deadline for this project is May of this year, and that goal is feeling more achievable than ever. HOMESICKNESS is now 95% complete, which is a huge milestone. There’s still so much I haven’t shown, and I’m keeping a lot under wraps to preserve the surprise.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/e749fea40fe14cb79f887944c540d15ef60cef04.png[/img]

There are only two things left to do before I can truly call the game "complete." However, I will be spending a decent amount of time ensuring it is as polished as possible before launch, as I want a perfect release in every aspect. The pricing has also been settled; the game will launch at $7.99, so look forward to that!

Developing this daily has been a huge task, and managing everything at once can be challenging. So just bear with me and expect the actual launch very, very soon. While the release timeframe could still change, I’m feeling very confident, having spent a significant amount of time planning, writing down stuff, and expanding the overall game content.

The game is definitely nearing completion, and what remains to be done is minimal compared to everything that’s already finished; core mechanics, most graphics, content, secrets, writing, and more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/a4a00e3ee17700b7163a26df1d42c6c635fb5aab.png[/img]

That said, the official release date will likely be announced very soon once the game goes gold. I can't stress enough how close I really am to that moment. This project is quite ambitious for a solo endeavor, packed with content, replay value, and plenty of hidden details to discover and analyze. 

I can’t wait to finally share it all in the full release; along with the upcoming launch trailer, which will tease some of the things I’ve been holding back!

In the meantime, if you'd like to stay up to date with HOMESICKNESS news and promo content, you can check out my socials (@jnitykit). If you have any questions, feel free to drop them below, and I'll answer them over time!

More news coming very soon. :)

notes.title: HOMESICKNESS — Developer Insight
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=eDNd5fd2eqQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Special thank you to celesware and Sam Schulthies

Hello everyone! Thank you for all the support on the HOMESICKNESS Steam page. I've been working pretty much daily over the past year to get to this point, leading up to 2025.

To give some more developer insight into this process, I wanted to write this entry; not only as the Steam page's first announcement but also to discuss my overall approach to this game and what I aspire to achieve with this solo-made project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/c41ba81651f1250efe3a4db6adb3768ac42c5720.gif[/img]

As previously mentioned, HOMESICKNESS has been in active development over the past year, starting in mid-2024 and remaining consistently in development until now. 

As already explained on the main Steam page, one of the core intentions of this project is to explore nostalgia through an abstract, surreal canvas that extends to every layer of the game itself.

This has been carefully thought out, and overall, I am confident in saying that it has been achieved to its potential. There is so much I'd like to talk about and so much I'd love to go into detail on when it comes to this game's core story and layer of ambiguity, but I aim to save what is, to me, one of the most important aspects of this game for the full release.

Every element of the game has been designed to work dynamically as a whole, serving as meaning for many of its inner themes and intricacies. And as of right now, the game is actually very close to completion!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/8be7138a45bea5696ca4f4a4702eb80ad1b73213.gif[/img]

If I had to give a rough estimate, I'd say about 80% of the game as a whole is complete. I am mainly in the polishing phase at this point, though there is still quite a bit left to do, far beyond the polishing phase. 

Working on this game entirely alone as a solo developer has taught me many things, and I am very glad I've been able to pull this off. Work will continue over the coming months, and though I can't give a definitive release date at the moment, my rough estimate is mid to late May. However, take this with a grain of salt, as it is not set in stone; just my approximate deadline.

This is, above all else, a deeply passionate project; one that I've poured so much of myself into. I can't wait for it to finally be released and for all the work to come to full fruition. I'm excited to share more, and I can't wait for everyone to play it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45547455/2e36531280f8b4730225658335643b32a00578d2.gif[/img]

As an adequate way to close off this post, I want to once again thank everyone for all the support given. This project has put my entire skillset to the test, drawing from years of developer knowledge. I've had to come to terms with so much as the sole developer of this project, but I promise it will absolutely live up to everything it is setting out to do. 

I want this project to fully live up to its concept, its purpose, and its goal of telling a deeply intricate, psychological tale. And ultimately, to be a solid game, with tons of gameplay working perfectly in harmony with its story and concept; without sacrificing the focus of either.

More news soon over the course of time! :)
